content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, building a line-by-line source ledger against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 17 claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-13 installed assembly, 14-17 method) were traced limitation by limitation to the disclosure: two semicircular frame halves, hinge end and latch end, three jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads that avoid a tool-specific diameter, carriage springs biasing outward, segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half, complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by frame closure, follower-in-oblique-slot synchronization, wedge on the latch bearing on a ring drive face, limited stroke, force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge, indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, first/over-center latch positions, mounting boss outside the annular guide not participating in synchronization, and the install/remove sequences. All 28 numerals in draft/numerals.md (10-66, with 28 unused) were checked: each has exactly one meaning, each appears in the detailed description, and each appears on at least one figure sheet; description cross-references (36 in FIG. 2; 54 in FIGS. 3 and 4; 38/40 in FIG. 5; 44/46/48/50 in FIG. 6; 52 in FIG. 4) match the sheet numeral lists. Hinge/latch handedness is internally consistent across sheets: hinge at the left break (FIG. 1), junctions left and right (FIGS. 3, 6), 44/46 as hinge-end faces at the left junction and 48/50 as latch-end faces at the right junction, first segment 32 = upper = first frame half 12. No section lines are named anywhere, so no designation-repetition conflict exists; FIG. 2 ("near-side structure omitted") and FIG. 4 ("cutaway") are described identically in the briefs and in draft/07-drawings.md. No placeholder, drafting note, open question, or unresolved alternative remains in any section, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" shape-justifying language leaked from a figure brief into the application text. Terminology is uniform between claims and description (ring drive face, oblique slot, follower, radial guide, carriage spring, force-limiting spring stack, latch housing, fixed edge, indicator pin, mounting boss). Abstract is 146 words, single paragraph, and adds nothing beyond the disclosure. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support statements match input/brief.md; the brief was used only for those formalities. The YOU passage in input/conversation.md describing a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" is drafting-agent prose, is not inventor support, and correctly appears nowhere in the draft. Two untraced substantive geometry assertions were found in the figure briefs and are reported: (1) the verbalized equal 120-degree angular spacing of the three carriages/slideways/slots, where the source says only that three carriages are "distributed around the closed frame" and the claims and description say only "distributed circumferentially"; and (2) the circumferential placement of the functional ring drive face 54 "adjacent the right junction" / at the break between the frame halves, which the source never locates relative to a segment junction. Items considered and accepted as depiction conventions (part disclosed, no undisclosed relationship verbalized, claims and description shape-neutral): the generic annular frame band, schematic hinge circle, rectangular latch housing with plain top wall, plain block wedge (no taper stated), zigzag carriage spring acting radially outward, plain straight end-face lines at the junctions with the narrow clearance expressly labelled a depiction convention confined to the figure brief, and the schematic radial placement of the cam ring within the frame annulus. Prior-art characterizations in draft/05-background.md were not traced to inventor support, per instruction; patentability, novelty, and validity were not assessed, and per input/brief.md no prior-art search was run so the art on hand may be incomplete.

findings.title: Figure briefs assert equal 120-degree angular spacing of the three jaw carriages and the three oblique slots, which the inventor never disclosed
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md (geometry, third bullet); figures/FIG-2.md (geometry, fourth bullet); figures/FIG-3.md (geometry, third bullet); figures/FIG-6.md (geometry, fifth bullet)
findings.detail: The briefs verbalize an exact angular proportion and relative location for the carriages, the slideways and the cam-ring slots. The disclosure states only the count and that the carriages are spread around the frame; it never states that they are equally spaced, nor that the spacing is one third of a turn. Equal 120-degree spacing is not a non-substantive page placement: it is a technical relationship (symmetric three-point centering of the pipe, equal slot phasing) that the claims and description deliberately do not recite - claim 1 and the description say only "distributed circumferentially about the frame". The drawing therefore asserts an invention relationship absent from the traced text. The count of three is disclosed and must be kept; only the equal-interval proportion is untraced.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording, FIG-2.md: "Exactly three slideways through the annular body, no more and no fewer, at equal angular intervals of about one third of a turn and clear of both breaks". FIG-3.md: "Exactly three elongated slots through the band, no more and no fewer, at equal angular intervals of about one third of a turn". FIG-6.md: "at equal angular intervals of about one third of a turn, and none of them at either junction". FIG-1.md: "Three carriage blocks at roughly equal angular intervals distributed circumferentially, none of them at either break." Nearest and only source passage (disclosure.md): "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame." No affirmative USER passage anywhere in disclosure.md or the USER message in conversation.md states equal angular intervals, one third of a turn, or any spacing value.
findings.fix: Delete the angular-proportion wording from all four briefs, keeping the disclosed count. In FIG-2.md write: "Exactly three slideways through the annular body, no more and no fewer, spaced apart from one another around the ring and clear of both breaks: one slideway at the top of the ring, one at the lower right and one at the lower left." In FIG-3.md write: "Exactly three elongated slots through the band, no more and no fewer, spaced apart from one another around the band and none of them at either junction: one slot at the top of the ring, one at the lower right and one at the lower left." In FIG-6.md write: "Exactly three elongated slots through the band, no more and no fewer, in the same positions and at the same inclinations as in FIG. 3, and none of them at either junction." In FIG-1.md write: "Three carriage blocks spaced apart from one another around the annular frame body, none of them at either break." Make no change to the claims, description, or draft/07-drawings.md, which are already free of any spacing recitation.

findings.title: Figure briefs place the functional ring drive face 54 at the junction between the cam-ring segments, a circumferential position the inventor never disclosed
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md (geometry, fourth bullet, and numeral target for 54); figures/FIG-6.md (geometry, last bullet); figures/FIG-4.md (geometry, fourth bullet)
findings.detail: Ring drive face 54 is a functional drive surface: the wedge acts on it to rotate the coupled ring. The briefs verbalize its circumferential position as "adjacent the right junction" and, in FIG. 4, as lying at the break where the two frame halves meet, i.e. at the abutting ends of the two cam-ring segments. That position carries technical substance because it fixes which cam-ring segment the wedge loads directly and whether the drive must pass across the abutting end faces 48/50 to reach the other segment - a load-path relationship the description and claims never state. The disclosure locates the drive face nowhere; it says only that the wedge is driven against a drive face of the cam ring. Under the functional-surface rule, a circumferential end position of a drive face is substantive even though the brief calls the face schematic, so the untraced locating words must be removed. The face itself is affirmatively disclosed and may remain as a minimally specific generic face at the latch end, since the wedge is carried by the latch and the latch is at the latch end.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording, FIG-3.md: "A short plain drive face on the band adjacent the right junction, at the latch end, where the wedge of the latch acts on the ring", and numeral target "54: the short plain drive face on the band adjacent the right junction." FIG-6.md: "A short plain drive face on the band adjacent the right junction, at the latch end, as in FIG. 3". FIG-4.md: "Visible through the break, beneath the housing, a short arcuate cam-ring portion drawn as two curved lines a short distance apart, carrying a short plain drive face where the wedge acts on it." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." No affirmative USER passage places the drive face adjacent, at, or across a junction between the cam-ring segments.
findings.fix: In FIG-3.md replace the bullet with: "A short plain drive face on the band at the latch end of the ring, where the wedge of the latch acts on the ring. The drive face is shown schematically; its outline is a depiction convention." and replace the numeral target with: "54: the short plain drive face on the band at the latch end." In FIG-6.md replace the bullet with: "A short plain drive face on the band at the latch end, as in FIG. 3, shown schematically and carrying no numeral on this sheet." In FIG-4.md replace the bullet with: "Beneath the housing, a short arcuate cam-ring portion drawn as two curved lines a short distance apart, carrying a short plain drive face where the wedge acts on it." No change is needed to the claims, description, or draft/07-drawings.md, which recite only that the wedge bears on a ring drive face of the cam ring.
